News.title: At least 20 firefighters taken to hospital & three fire engines destroyed in Essex fire after massive explosion
News.content:
AT LEAST 20 firefighters have been injured and three fire engines destroyed following an explosion that ripped through an industrial site.

At 5pm yesterday, Essex County Fire and Rescue Service raced to battle a fire in East Hanningfield, Essex, on Southend Road.



After declaring a major incident, over 100 firefighters attended the scene.

At least 20 firefighters were taken to hospital following the incident, with four suffering minor injuries.



The remainder were precautionary assessments, including checks for issues such as hearing loss following the explosion.

All those firefighters have now been discharged from hospital.

News.title: I was sold as sex slave after traffickers held me at gunpoint – how I escaped to convict them in real-life Taken raid
News.content:
SEX SLAVE HELL I was sold as sex slave after traffickers held me at gunpoint – how I escaped to convict them in real-life Taken raid

ALARM bells rang in Shandra Woworuntu’s mind as she saw condoms scattered across the floor of a filthy New York attic on the first day of her new job.

But moments later things took another sinister turn for the young mum as her boss asked her to undress – before pointing a gun to her head.



What followed was years of abuse at the hands of twisted sex traffickers who sold off Shandra to hundreds of men who raped her.

She managed to escape on several occasions but was never free for long until a chance meeting with a US Navy officer led to a real-life Taken-style raid involving the FBI, a team of snipers and a slew of convictions.





Shandra had left Indonesia for the US in 2001, then aged 24, to escape a crippling financial crisis that cost her her job as a banker.

An advert in a newspaper sold her the dream of a hospitality gig for a top hotel in Chicago, a place Shandra had fallen in love with after watching American romance movies and listening to Whitney Houston.

Leaving behind her three-year-old daughter, Tania, she was promised a salary of $5,000 (£3,740) a month, with accommodation provided.

Flights were quickly booked as an excited Shandra landed at JFK Airport believing she would then be taken 800 miles across to Illinois.



As the plane wheels hit the tarmac, her dreams of a better life felt like they were finally coming true.

Within minutes of meeting her new boss, known as Johnny Wong, it became an unimaginable nightmare.

Shandra had unknowingly been trafficked to the US and was now expected to have forced sex at least 20 times a day by her sick captors.



The now 50-year-old told The Sun: “When I landed at JFK there were six of us and it was split into two groups, one male with two girls and then I was with another two girls.

“One was around 17 or 18-years-old and the other one was 15-years-old. I was 24, the oldest, and became the leader of that group.

“They took us to a place in Queens, New York, in front of a hotel. I thought it was Chicago, I didn’t know.

“I was looking at the window and someone handed a big envelope of money to Wong, who took it and told us I have to go with these people and stay overnight, and that we cannot travel to Chicago.”

Shandra said she followed the instructions still hoping she was heading to her hospitality job.



The girls were dragged inside a building and marched to the top floor as Shandra’s heart sank when the door was flung open.

“The room was huge and there was a king or queen sized bed. It was filthy and I thought ‘why is it so dirty’,” she recalled.

“On the bed sheet, there was a stain – a dirty spot. I saw some used condoms on the floor and a side table by the bed.



“I saw new condoms with different styles. I thought, ‘what kind of place is this?’”

After being left alone in the room with the other girls for a few minutes, a burly man came in and demanded the women undress.

“He didn’t speak English well. I understood what he wanted but I couldn’t answer him very well. I just said no,” she added.

“I asked why he wanted to see my body and to see me naked. When I said no a few times, he took his gun and pointed it on my forehead.”

At that moment, Shandra’s blood ran cold.



She was in a state of shock and knew she had to make a choice – do as her new employers asked or face being killed.

Shandra was led to a separate room and forced to undress so the men could look over her body and check for any tattoos or markings.

She was then bundled into a car and driven to a new location with a gun pointed at her waist the entire journey.

A man grabbed her wrists and led her to a building where two men spoke for a brief moment – and Shandra remembers hearing the phrase “Mama-san, a new girl”.

She later learned that Mama-san is a term said to those who run a sex business, often a woman known as mama.



Shandra continued: “I went inside and saw a big man with a baseball bat in the corner as this lady said ‘you will start working’.”

After a short stay in the house of horrors, where men would come in and out with a host of drugs, Shandra heard that she had been “sold”.

She said: “I couldn’t think of anything other than that I had to comply because of the gun and baseball bat. My life was on the line.”

Her traffickers set a cruel, fabricated debt of $30,000 on Shandra’s head and said each time she had sex they would deduct $100 from the sum.

That meant she was staring at the nauseating prospect of having non-consensual sex 300 times.



She added: “I was sold and I didn’t earn anything, so it wasn’t a type of work. It was rape.

“My trafficker made money but I didn’t get anything but abuse.

“They created a debt on my body. My trafficker told me ‘you have to pay $30,000 for the job that I gave you’. It wasn’t a job. It was rape.

“And the buyers didn’t care. The more I screamed, the more abuse I received.”



The devious nature of the seedy men paying for sex also meant they would often pay once but keep Shandra for hours.

At this point she was using drugs to help cope with the abuse.

She continued: “Twenty-four hours a day I was expected to have sex in brothels, hotels and working as an escort.

“The drugs helped me to survive. To be numb. Not feel anything. And my mind was thinking about my daughter and just staying one day at a time.”



Deciding she couldn’t go on, Shandra began to plot her escape.

The first time she broke free she called a number given to her by a woman working at the house.

She was told to escape the trafficker’s home and call the number as soon as she was safely out of sight.

Fleeing the sex compound was hard enough as they were on the second floor of a tall home so she had to risk her life by jumping out of a bathroom window.

Once outside, she quickly phoned the number – which led her to a friend of Wong, the man who had first picked her up from JFK Airport.



Shandra was caught and forced back to her life of forced sex and drug use.

The second time she escaped proved more successful as she again fled the home and managed to evade being caught.

She was homeless for months in New York and left begging for food and cash.

Eventually, a US Navy officer on holiday noticed her in tears and put her in touch with the FBI.

They launched a full-scale investigation into the illegal sex brothel with Shandra’s help and pulled off a dramatic raid using her knowledge.



She explained the Taken-style operation saw her put inside an FBI van and led across NYC until they passed the home she had spent months inside.

After alerting the special ops team Shandra said: “They stopped. The whole team gathered and they moved me into a smaller car.

“Someone stayed with me and said ‘stay here. Don’t look back’.

“But I was curious, so I looked back to see what happened. I saw many people surrounding the building.

The undercover officers had guns, with snipers surrounding the location. It was like a movie. They went in by force.”



After swarming the brothel, Shandra was asked to identify the perpetrators as a dozen people were arrested.

Wong was eventually convicted for trafficking along with two other men thanks to Shandra’s testimony.

The proud mum was reunited with her daughter, and they now live together in New York.

She is now a human rights activist after founding the survivors group, Mentari.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In 2017, she was awarded a L’Oreal Woman of Worth award and made a speech outside the White House in 2015 with then Representative Carolyn Maloney.



She copes with her trauma through a combination of therapy and medication, but admits the grim flashbacks continue to this day.

News.title: Net zero leaves Britain at risk of BLACKOUTS & higher bills, warns leaked National Grid report
News.content:
LEFT IN THE DARK Net zero leaves Britain at risk of BLACKOUTS & higher bills, warns leaked National Grid report

THE government’s net zero goals could lead to higher energy bills and increased risks of blackouts, warns a leaked report.

The National Grid are reportedly “flying blind” as it’s unable to predict supply and demand due to the rise in green energy suppliers.

A confidential report for the National Energy System Operator (Neso) revealed that it cannot accurately predict supply and demand, reports The Times.



A whistleblower disclosed the report to the paper – which reportedly found that wind farms, solar panels and batteries, do not have to engage with Neso.



But Neso insisted the report was “forward looking” and that the UK’s energy network was “one of the most reliable in the world”, while the government said they are “very confident” in the UK’s supply.

If green energy suppliers do not have to engage with Neso, this means it is unable to keep the energy network stable, leaving the country at a greater risk of high electricity bills and blackouts.

Neso may have to pay more to manage its services at short notice if they cannot predict demand, which would lead to higher costs for consumers.

Last month, the National Grid breached five safety limits during heatwave due to green energy making it difficult to balance demand.

On June 23, the electricity grid’s security system was breached, along with five operational safety constraints.



Ofgem has since announced an investigation into the June 23 incident.

Neso commissioned the report to Cornwall Insight, an energy consultancy group, which revealed issues with monitoring and forecasting the energy network.

The rise of green energy means the control room has “reduced visibility of the capacity which is supplying and taking power from the GB network”.

The leaked report estimated that by 2030, the amount of invisible energy could reach 7.7GW – the equivalent to the output of two big nuclear power stations.

One control room whistleblower said that these issues have been know to engineers for two years, and yet they feel they are have not been listened to.



They claimed Neso was “flying blind, every minute of every day. We are risking total blackout.”

They added: “We don’t have an opinion on net zero, we just want the system to be safe, but the execs are too scared politically to say renewables are making the system unsafe.

“It will get worse week by week because we are connecting more things that we cannot model.”

Claire Coutinho, the shadow energy secretary, has raised the concerns of whistleblowers to the new energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh about the increasingly complex electricity system.

She wrote to the Fahnbulleh to demand answers about the issues that the push for net zero could cause.



Fahnbulleh has previously called for Britain to race towards Net Zero by 2034 and would rely on spending taxpayers’ cash on expensive wind farms and eco-energy grids.

A Neso spokesman told The Times that Britain had “one of the most reliable electricity systems in the world” and described Cornwall Insight’s report as a “forward-looking” assessment of risks that could become more significant during the 2030s unless addressed.

A programme of work to implement the recommendations was under way, according to the spokesman.

He said the findings had been shared with the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Ofgem and a Neso board committee.

The government said: “Neso is responsible for planning and delivering the energy system now, and into the future.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As part of that, it plans for emerging challenges to ensure Britain continues to benefit from a secure energy system.

“We are very confident in our security of supply arrangements, and that Neso have the tools they need to manage the system.”

News.title: D4vd’s teen victim got pregnant & had abortion at 13 before ‘singer stabbed her to death’, chilling texts appear to show
News.content:
DARK TWIST D4vd’s teen victim got pregnant & had abortion at 13 before ‘singer stabbed her to death’, chilling texts appear to show

D4VD’S alleged teen victim got pregnant and had an abortion at 13 years old before she was stabbed to death, chilling texts appear to show.

The singer is accused of murdering 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez and abandoning her dismembered body in a Tesla trunk in Los Angeles.



Dozens of alarming photographs and texts were shown at a hearing to determine whether the singer, real name David Anthony Burke, should stand trial for her death.

“Both of us aren’t able to take care of it,” Celeste wrote to D4vd on January 8, 2024.



“I know but still,” he responded, before apologising for “putting her through this”.

She replied, writing: “neither of us are capable of watching and taking care of the baby. it’s for the best no?”



Burke then asked: “my mother always told me to ask this question if I was ever in this situation … it is mine right?

Celeste responded: “of course its yours David,” according to a detective’s testimony.



The court heard of another exchange in June of that year, when Celeste was 13-years-old and Burke 19.

“What [if] the first abortion didn’t work?” she asked, according to prosecutors.

Burke wrote: “Let’s let this abortion be the last one til we have the real one…”



The pair are also said to have discussed when the abortion would happen.

“When you gonna get it done?” Burke allegedly asked.

“Two days,” Rivas responded.

Burke’s device also contained photos of Celeste during the alleged sexual abuse, prosecutors said on Friday.

He allegedly stared directly at gruesome photos shown in court of Celeste Rivas’ decapitated and decomposed remains that were found stuffed in a body bag.



Celeste’s mother, Mercedes Rivas Hernandez, became visibly emotional and had to be led from the court as details of some of the pictures were described.

Burke met Celeste online in January 2022 when she was just 11 years old and began a sexual relationship with her when she was 13, court filing alleged.

At the time, Burke was an 18-year-old with a record deal after his breakout single, Romantic Homicide, successfully cracked the Billboard Hot 100 chart.

Burke was arrested on April 16, eight months after Celeste’s decomposed remains were uncovered in Hollywood.

The singer has pleaded not guilty to first-degree murder with special circumstances, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14, and unlawful mutilation of human remains.



Prosecutors said Burke fatally stabbed Celeste with a sharp object on April 23, 2025, at his rented home in the Hollywood Hills in order to cover up his sexual abuse of the teenager.

He feared his sexual crimes against her would ruin his career, prosecutors said during his arraignment in April.

“Knowing he had to silence the victim before she ruined his music career as she had threatened, very soon after her arrival at his home, the defendant stabbed the victim to death multiple times and stood by while she bled out,” prosecutors said.

As Celeste bled out, Burke allegedly mutilated her remains with two chainsaws he purchased on Amazon in an inflatable pool in his garage.

Prosecutors allege Burke later stored her remains in the front trunk of his Tesla and went on tour.



Officials said Burke took “horrifying measures to destroy and discard the victim’s body.”

Prosecutors obtained text messages between Burke and Celeste on the night they believe she was murdered.

“The messages reveal the victim’s jealousy over defendant’s relationship with other women, as defendant led her to believe they had a future together,” court documents read.

“She became extremely upset and threatened to disclose damaging information about her relationship with defendant to end his career and destroy his life.”

The preliminary hearing is expected to last several days and a judge will determine whether prosecutors have enough evidence to take Burke to trial.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Burke faces the death penalty, if he goes to trial and is convicted. He is being held without bail.

News.title: Rampaging killer whales cripple another yacht as orcas terrorise Spanish coast with 5 attacks in just 48 hours
News.content:
A POD of killer whales has terrorised yet another vessel off the coast of Spain in their latest attack.

Two people aboard the 45ft Swedish-flagged yacht called Vai were forced to send a Mayday after their rudder was smashed.



An alarm was raised at 1.15pm on Friday as the orcas rammed into them 13 miles to the northwest of Punta Candelaria, a lighthouse near the fishing town of Celeiro.

A Spanish Coastguard vessel raced to their rescue and towed the yacht to the town of Viveiro.



“The vessel Mar de Galicia is towing a 14-metre yacht flying the Swedish flag towards Celeiro with two people on board due to a rudder failure after an interaction with orcas northwest of Punta Candelaria,” they said.

Rescuers were involved in four attacks involving killer whales on Thursday.



In the most dramatic incident, two people on board a pleasure craft called Idem had to be rescued after their rudder was destroyed and they started to sink.

The ramming happened at 5pm on Thursday over a mile off Estaca de Bares, the northernmost cape of the Iberian Peninsula, which is also part of the province of La Coruna.

Local mayor Alfredo Dovale said a private boat aided the sailors and tried to tow their yacht to shore before it started disappearing under the sea.

In the other three interactions with orcas the same day in the same area, the rudders of three yachts were also targeted.



But the damage done did not prevent them from reaching shore in two of the cases although in the other one the yacht was also crippled.

Spanish coastguards said about the attacks: “A yacht has sunk 1.3 miles from Estaca de Bares as a result of taking on water after an interaction with orcas.

“Its two crew members were picked up by a nearby motorboat and are safe.



“Later, the rescue vessel Shaula, dispatched by CCS Finisterre, transported them to Carino. The Helimer 401 helicopter is flying over the area to check for any signs of pollution.”

A second message confirmed the fourth orca interaction that occurred in the area.

“While assisting the yacht Idem, it emerged another sailing vessel had also experienced an interaction with these marine mammals, but the damage to its rudder was minimal and it continued sailing to Viveiro,” they said.

Last October, the Portuguese Air Force had to rescue a family of five including three children after they cheated death when their yacht was attacked by an orca.

A military helicopter was mobilised to winch the survivors off a fishing vessel that had come to their rescue after their boat was rammed by a pod of mammals and started taking on water.



They were taken by chopper to hospital although they were not injured in the drama, which occurred late on October 10, 55 miles south-east of Peniche, a 75-minute drive north of Lisbon.

Three children aged eight, ten and 12 were on board the French-flagged 36ft-long yacht, named locally as Ti’fare, with their mum and dad when it was attacked.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Their parents managed to send an SOS and get into a life raft before the vessel started sinking.

A Peniche-based fishing boat called Silmar responded to the alert as the military were mobilised.

News.title: Moment gang of brazen kids raid corner shop as exhausted owner says shoplifting is ‘worse than ever’
News.content:
THIS is the moment a gang of brazen kids pilfered a corner shop as CCTV footage captured his business being looted four times in one week.

Footage shows the relentless youths emptying shelves and stuffing items into their pockets.



Exhausted shopkeeper Krish Hinglajia said shoplifting is “worse than ever” with his shop raided by youths several times in a week, costing him hundreds of pounds.

The 38-year-old shopkeeper has been targeted by gangs of children nicking chocolates, sweets and ice creams.



He said he’s lost up to £200 in a week – with sweets and ice creams in particular being pilfered.

It comes as the government has vowed to crackdown on shoplifting after a surge in the petty crime post-pandemic.

He said: “We have lost more than £150 to £200 worth of goods in the last week, particularly on frozen foods, which are really expensive.

“That has a deep impact on my business because we are a small family-run shop.



“At the end of the day, if tills are getting low, how are we going to pay our bills?”

The incidents have been reported to police with a total of 128 shoplifting related crimes reported in the area between June 2025 and May 2026.

Despite reporting the recent incidents twice, Krish says officers did not attend and was told to put his details into an online portal for an investigation to take place.

He said: “We are just losing faith, why are we paying council tax that goes towards funding the police if we are not receiving their service?”

A spokesperson for the force confirmed it is investigating reports that a group of children has committed multiple thefts at a shop.



Inspector Paul Relf said: “When the business owner reported the incidents, he was requested to submit relevant CCTV footage via an online portal to assist identifying the suspects.

“We are determined to tackle retail crime in Medway and will pursue all available lines of enquiry to track down offenders and bring them to justice.”

News.title: Southport killer is trying to ‘retraumatise families from his cell’ by playing the system, says victims’ lawyer
News.content:
MANIPULATIVE KILLER Southport killer is trying to ‘retraumatise families from his cell’ by playing the system, says victims’ lawyer

THE Southport murderer is trying “to retraumatise the families from his cell”, the victims’ lawyer said.

Axel Rudakubana, who is serving a 52-year life sentence for killing three girls, was earlier this week transferred from Belmarsh Prison to Broadmoor Hospital nearly two years on from the horror attack.



Rudakubana, now 19, murdered Alice da Silva Aguiar, nine, Bebe King, six, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and attempted the murder of eight other children and two adults.

It’s been nearly two years since he carried out the attack at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class on July 29, 2024.



It was confirmed by the Ministry of Justice that the killer was transferred to the category A psychiatric facility.

Chris Walker, who is representing the three bereaved families, told BBC Breakfast that this decision highlighted a concerning “pattern” in Rudakubana’s behaviour that is “retraumatising” for the victims’ families.

Walker said: “It’s a deep concern of mine that this is a pattern starting to develop by him trying to retraumatise the families from his cell, and it’s a deep concern that this is going to occur every anniversary.”

He also pointed out that there was “no suggestion” that Rudakubana was under any form of “psychosis” when he carried out the murders.



The families were only informed of the decision in a letter on July 22, but were not given details on why the transfer happened.

Walker said: “With the vacuum of information, the concern is that he’s manipulating the situation to his own benefit.”

He added: “For it to come out the week before the anniversary seems coincidental to us.

“Whether that’s been poorly handled by the Government, or whether it’s designed by him.”

Sally Jameson, a junior housing minister and former prison officer, said on Friday that Rudakubana would be returned to prison “as soon as possible” but that she was not familiar with why the decision had been taken to move him.



Offenders who present an increased risk, and cannot be managed safely in a prison environment because of mental disorders, can be moved to secure psychiatric units like Broadmoor.

People in these units are treated as patients rather than prisoners.

The Sun revealed that Rudakubana will live in a university hall-style room – and be free to spend his days at Broadmoor reading, watching films and TV and writing to friends and relatives.

The triple child killer will also have access to a state of the art gym, an on-site cafe and shop and even the hospital’s resident hairdresser and dentist.

Walker said: “When he did what he did, it was carefully planned, it was meticulous and it was designed to cause the maximum distress to society.



“There’s no evidence of any mental health disorder being a component of his crime. There’s no evidence of psychosis.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The families say, given that, he needs to serve a prison sentence, he should not be going to hospital. He needs to be in prison.”

Walker said that the letter included the offer of a meeting with the Director for Public Protection, which he will attend on behalf of the families.

News.title: Henry Nowak killer ‘literally shaking with fear’ at ‘Monster Mansion’ jail as bloodthirsty lags have target on his back
News.content:
HENRY Nowak’s killer is said to be “literally shaking with fear” behind bars after becoming a target for some of Britain’s most dangerous inmates.

Vickrum Digwa, 23, is locked up inside HMP Frankland in County Durham, the notorious high-security jail – nicknamed “Monster Mansion” – where he is being monitored over fears he could be attacked.



The prison is home to some of Britain’s most violent killers and terrorists – including Sarah Everard‘s murderer Wayne Couzens, serial killer Levi Bellfield and Lee Rigby killer Michael Adebolajo.

Digwa is said to have arrived there “terrified”, a source told the Daily Mail.



The sicko was transferred to Frankland from HMP Winchester after being jailed for life last month for murdering Southampton University student Henry Nowak.

He must serve a minimum of 21 years – though last month The Sun revealed Nowak’s killer would have his “lenient” jail sentence reviewed after the case sparked fury across the nation.



The source said: “Digwa arrived at Frankland terrified. I mean literally shaking. He was in total fear. There was none of that arrogance you saw on the police camera.

“I think he thought he wouldn’t survive the first night.”



After spending several weeks in segregation, Digwa has now been moved onto a prison wing but remains under close supervision because of the risks he faces.

The source said: “He is on a special watch list because of the recent murders in Frankland and he fits into the category of people who are at risk because of the nature of his crime and the fact that he is now a high-profile prisoner.

“There are cons in Frankland who will have a go at him, physically as well as verbally, because of who he is and so they can boast that they were the one who beat the s*** out of him.”

The insider claimed Digwa’s fearful body language has made him appear vulnerable.

Former prison governor Vanessa Frake-Harris said high-profile prisoners often become targets.



She said: “High-profile prisoners like Vickrum Digwa will always be targets. There are many in Frankland with nothing to lose but a lot of credibility to gain.

“His was a high-profile murder which angered society. This anger may well follow him into HMP Frankland.”

Jurors heard at Southampton Crown Court that Henry was walking home after a night out on December 3 last year when he crossed paths with Digwa.



The killer, carrying an eight-inch dagger around his neck, stabbed the student in the chest before inflicting four more wounds, including two to his back as Henry tried to run away.

Digwa tried to portray himself as the victim of a racist attack and failed to tell officers he had just repeatedly stabbed Henry.

Police bodycam captured the student’s final moments as he pleaded that he could not breathe.

Digwa was convicted of murder and possessing a knife in public before being jailed for life.

His mother, Kiran Kaur, was also convicted after taking the murder weapon from the scene and hiding it at the family home.



She is serving her sentence at HMP Bronzefield in Surrey, where fellow inmates include Lucy Letby, Constance Marten and Sara Sharif‘s killer Beinash Batool.

She and her sicko son are separated by around 300 miles having once sharing the same Southampton home.

Under Labour’s proposed sentencing reforms, which are currently under review, Kaur could potentially be released before the end of the year after time spent on remand is taken into account.



It comes as video footage has revealed the moment murderer Vickrum Digwa told his mother to take the knife he used to kill Henry away from the crime scene.

The Crown Prosecution Service released the clip after Digwa’s mother, Kiran Kaur, was jailed last Friday for assisting an offender.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In the footage taken on Digwa’s phone, which is pointed at the ground, he can be heard speaking to Kaur in Punjabi, asking her to remove the knife.

She then took it back to the family home.

News.title: UK weather model shows 45C heat surge in what would be hottest day ever seen
News.content:
UK weather model shows 45C heat surge in what would be hottest day ever seen

Weather forecasters say temperatures are expected to surge across Europe and in the UK next week - and one model suggests record-breaking 45C highs are possible

View 2 Images Temperatures are expected to surge well above the seasonal average next week (Image: WXCHARTS)

Weather modelling data suggests the UK could see what would be - by far - the hottest day in British history next week.

‌



One data set from the GEFS weather model shows staggering highs of 45C are on the cards in the south-east, in and around London, on Thursday.

‌



If that were to come to fruition, it would comfortably be the hottest day ever seen in the UK. The current all-time temperature record stands at 40.3C.

‌



That temperature record was set during the sweltering July 2022 heatwave - which was the first time ever that the mercury surpassed 40C in Britain. Highs of 45C would be unheard of.

View 2 Images The GEFS model suggests temperatures could reach 45C on Thursday (Image: Weather Outlook)

UK weather maps show 40C heatwave within days as 18 counties hit 39C or more READ MORE :

UK weather maps show heatwave reaching 37C in seven counties within six days READ MORE :

It should be noted that it is only one data set from one weather model that shows 45C is possible - so it remains unlikely. However, other weather models suggest temperatures could hit 39C or 40C next week.

‌



Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office says “very warm weather” is expected to return to some parts of the UK next week, with the fourth heatwave of the year likely.

“Many parts of England and Wales are likely to return to the mid to high-20s early next week, with the potential for temperatures to reach 30C again in southern and eastern England by Tuesday,” the national weather agency said.

“Conditions in the southeast could become very warm or locally hot, with the possibility that some locations may once again reach heatwave criteria, potentially making this the fourth heatwave episode of the year for parts of the UK.”

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

The Met Office forecast issued this morning predicts highs of 31C in southern areas on Tuesday and Wednesday. Northern regions could see highs of 28C across both days. The Met Office is yet to issue temperature predictions for the latter half of the week.

BBC weather forecast

The BBC forecast for Monday to Wednesday states: “Dry, sunny and very warm in the south and east on Monday and Tuesday but cloudy in the north and west with patchy rain at times.

Article continues below

“Wednesday will continue sunny and dry in the south. Further north will become sunnier, though showers may affect the north-west in the morning.”
