World.title: Polish president renews bid for referendum on EU climate policy
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has submitted a second request to parliament for a nationwide referendum on whether Poland should continue implementing the European Union’s climate policies, which he argues are too costly. Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, first proposed a referendum in May. But it was rejected by the Senate, the upper house of parliament, where the more liberal government has a majority. Senators argued that the proposed referendum question was “absurd”. The president has now submitted a revised proposal featuring a simplified question and again proposed holding the referendum on 27 September this year. Nawrocki’s originally proposed question was: “Are you in favour of implementing EU climate policy, which has led to an increase in citizens’ cost of living, energy prices and the cost of running business and agricultural activity?” However, following criticism in the Senate that the question was clearly intended to elicit a specific answer, this time he has proposed a more neutral one: “Are you in favour of Poland implementing the European Union’s climate policy?” “I’m looking for compromises, looking for solutions,” said Nawrocki on Thursday while announcing the new referendum bid. “The Senate wasn’t satisfied with the [previous] question”, so “we prepared a different one…[that] does not suggest anything”. However, the president has also proposed that the ballot paper would include information on what answering “yes” or “no” would mean in practice. Voters would be told, for example, that maintaining EU climate policy would result in, among other things, “Poland bearing costs estimated at 3.5 trillion zloty by 2040”, “burdens on agriculture”, “increasing costs for industry” and “obligations for owners of buildings”. By contrast, voting “no” would mean “negotiating exceptions and exemptions for Poland with the relevant EU bodies that will protect Polish industry and citizens from the burdens of climate policy”. Poland's right-wing opposition wants to withdraw from the EU Emissions Trading System, saying it makes Poles "a cash machine for absurd leftist climate policies"@PStrzalkowski explains what costs ETS really brings, and what prospects there are for reform https://t.co/UxpMWpG1pE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 4, 2026 Under Poland’s constitution, the president may call a referendum with the approval of a majority of senators in a vote where at least half of all members of the 100-seat chamber are present. The ruling coalition of Prime Minister Donald Tusk controls 63 seats in the Senate, making approval of proposals brought forward by Nawrocki, who often clashes with the government and regularly vetoes its bills, unlikely. While the government is generally pro-EU, it has also been critical of Brussels’ green policies, arguing that they place too great a burden on Poland. After the European Commission last Friday unveiled changes intended to soften the impact of the Emissions Trading Scheme (ETS), the EU’s flagship climate policy, they were welcomed by the Polish government as a step in the right direction. Dzisiaj robimy milowy krok w zmianie systemu ETS. Po raz pierwszy Komisja Europejska proponuje rozwiązania, które łagodzą, a nie zaostrzają wpływ systemu na gospodarkę i obywateli. To efekt konsekwentnych działań Polski i zbudowania silnej koalicji państw w UE. Dzisiejsza… pic.twitter.com/5AMd9KCBVa — Ministerstwo Klimatu i Środowiska (@MKiS_GOV_PL) July 17, 2026 However, in his written justification for the new referendum proposal, Nawrocki wrote that, while he had “given the government time” in its push for ETS reform, the final result was simply “technical adjustments” that postpone some elements but do “not change the direction” or ultimate outcome. “ETS will remain an increasingly expensive, increasingly extensive system, and increasingly burdensome for the Polish economy,” wrote the president. The national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which is the main opposition and supported Nawrocki’s bid for the presidency last year, wants Poland to unilaterally withdraw from ETS. Government figures warn, however, that there is no way to do so without either accruing enormous fines or leaving the EU entirely. When in power, PiS launched a revolution in Poland's energy transition. But now, in opposition, it has disowned those achievements and returned to an emphasis on coal. This could be a missed opportunity to win back centrist voters, writes @OrzelBartlomiej https://t.co/8cGvubn7N2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 29, 2026 Nawrocki’s new referendum proposal was met with criticism by figures from the ruling coalition. “There is no possibility of one country suspending part of EU law,” wrote Stanisław Gawłowski, a senator from Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO) party. “This referendum is pure fraud.” Foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, also from KO, wrote that, “as the Brits have learned, the Europhobe’s dream world, in which one enjoys all the privileges of EU membership without any obligations, does not exist”. However, Nawrocki’s initiative was welcomed by Przemysław Czarnek, deputy leader of PiS, who wrote that, “on such fundamental matters as climate policy, Poles should decide, not Brussels bureaucrats”. Zaproponowane przez @NawrockiKn pytanie referendalne jest wybiórcze. Kontrpropozycja: „Czy jesteś za likwidacją unijnych dopłat do inwestycji i dla rolników?” Jak przekonali się Brytyjczycy, świat eurofoba, w którym ma się same przywileje członkostwa w UE, nie istnieje. — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) July 23, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland appoints new human rights commissioner
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The government’s majority in parliament has chosen Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram as Poland’s new human rights commissioner. She will take office after the five-year term of the incumbent, Marcin Wiącek, expires today. Gregorczyk-Abram is a prominent lawyer and activist, who is particularly well known for opposing the overhaul of the judiciary by the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. PiS, which is now the main opposition party, strongly opposed her election, arguing that she is politically aligned with the current, more liberal government. Gregorczyk-Abram herself, however, has pledged to “put all my beliefs and views aside” when she takes up the new role. Senat wyraził zgodę na powołanie Sylwii Gregorczyk-Abram na Rzecznika Praw Obywatelskich. pic.twitter.com/gz3rwGy3hi — Senat RP 🇵🇱 (@PolskiSenat) July 22, 2026 The commissioner for human rights (widely known by its Polish initials, RPO) is appointed by a resolution of the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, with the consent of the upper-house Senate. Candidates must meet certain requirements, including not belonging to any political party and having legal expertise and relevant experience. As well as acting as a watchdog for human rights, the RPO also has the power to submit motions to the Constitutional Tribunal to assess the constitutionality of laws and to file so-called cassation appeals to the Supreme Court and Supreme Administrative Court against rulings by lower courts. Poland’s human rights commissioner has written to the government expressing concern that a "temporary" ban on asylum claims by most migrants who irregularly cross the border from Belarus remains in place after more than a year https://t.co/9SA2TypQdK — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 28, 2026 Gregorczyk-Abram was last month nominated as a candidate to be the new RPO by the main ruling party, Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO), along with one of its coalition partners, The Left (Lewica). PiS proposed a rival candidate, Adam Borowski, a veteran of Poland’s anti-communist struggle in the 1980s. However, critics argued that Borowski, an activist and former PiS election candidate, does not appear to have the requisite legal knowledge and experience. In a Sejm vote last Friday, the ruling coalition supported Gregorczyk-Abram, who won 233 votes to Borowski’s 177. On Wednesday, her candidacy was also supported by the Senate, with 59 votes in favour and 25 against, confirming that she will become the new RPO. Gregorczyk-Abram is best known as one of the founders and leaders of the Free Courts (Wolne Sądy) initiative launched in 2017 amid a wave of protests against the then-PiS government’s efforts to take greater control over the judiciary. Free Courts was prominent in efforts to defend the rule of law. Many of its leading figures are now associated with the current ruling coalition: Maria Ejchart is a deputy justice minister, while Michał Wawrykiewicz is a member of the European Parliament representing KO. In April last year, Gregorczyk-Abram was made chairwoman of a commission established by the current government to look into cases of abuse of power against civil society under the former PiS administration. In September, her commission published its first findings, in which it said that public media outlets under PiS control had “carried out systematic repressive and defamatory actions against activists, non-governmental organisations, and civil society”. Poland's public media “carried out systematic repressive actions against activists, NGOs and civil society” during the rule of the former PiS government, a report commissioned by the new government has found https://t.co/S2MO9KGssC — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 26, 2025 PiS argues that Gregorczyk-Abram’s previous activity makes her unsuitable as a suitable candidate for RPO, which is meant to be a non-partisan role. They also point to claims that she was involved in a group of legal figures that discussed the Tusk government’s controversial takeover of public media in December 2023. “[She] is a discredited and extremely politicised person who should be brought to justice, and not receive the laurels of the commissioner for human rights,” former PiS justice minister Marcin Warchoł told the Do Rzeczy weekly last month. After a Sejm committee hearing on Gregorczyk-Abram’s candidacy earlier this month, former PiS deputy justice minister Sebastian Kaleta criticised her for ignoring questions over her alleged “role in the illegal takeover of public media”. Zadałem Sylwii Gregorczyk-Abram serię pytań o jej działania i możliwe spotkania z Ewą Wrzosek w sprawie przejęcia TVP, w tym możliwego tworzenia dokumentów prokuratorskich w prywatnej kancelarii. Kandydatka ostentacyjnie zdecydowała się ignorować te pytania. Ma bardzo dużo do… — Sebastian Kaleta (@sjkaleta) July 15, 2026 Speaking to state broadcaster TVP on Wednesday after her appointment was confirmed by the Senate, Gregorczyk-Abram declared that, “from the moment I take the oath and assume the position of commissioner, I will be independent and sovereign”. She pledged to “put all my beliefs and views – because each of us has them – aside and become an advocate for all citizens, regardless of what they believe in, how they live, or who they vote for”. Gregorczyk-Abram said that among her priorities as RPO would be the justice system, supporting the rights of disabled people and their carers, protecting older people, and fighting hate speech. With regard to the last of these issues, she noted that certain politicians present some groups as “enemies”, pointing to how this previously happened with LGBT+ people and judges, and is now being directed towards Ukrainians. Those are all groups who have at various stages been targeted by PiS and other right-wing parties. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland is up 30% so far this year, police data show. The figures come following recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians, who are Poland's largest immigrant group https://t.co/pcTsJddDz7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: President to swear in new judge to Poland’s disputed constitutional court
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has agreed to swear in a new judge to the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), ending weeks of doubt as to whether the opposition-aligned president would accept the judge appointed by the government’s parliamentary majority. Although Sławomir Patyra will now be accepted onto the court, four other judges appointed by parliament earlier this year continue to be excluded after Nawrocki refused to receive their oaths and the TK’s chief justice, also aligned with the opposition, blocked them from taking office. W najbliższy wtorek 28 lipca Prezydent Karol Nawrocki działając na postawie art. 4 ust. 1 ustawy o statusie sędziów Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, przyjmie ślubowanie od prof. Sławomira Patyry i tego samego dnia wręczy powołania czterem nowym sędziom Sądu Najwyższego. W przyszłym… — Zbigniew Bogucki🇵🇱 (@BoguckiZbigniew) July 22, 2026 Under Polish law, when a vacancy emerges among the 15 positions on the TK – for example when a judge’s nine-year term expires – the lower house of parliament, the Sejm, chooses who should fill it. However, to take office, the judge must swear an oath before the president. In April, after the Sejm had chosen six candidates to fill vacancies on the court, Nawrocki took the unprecedented step of inviting only two of them to be sworn in. He argued there were doubts over the legality of how all six had been chosen, but decided to accept two to ensure the TK had the necessary quorum to function. Those two have been able to take up their seats on the court, but the other four remain in limbo. Although they arranged their own private swearing-in ceremony without the presence of Nawrocki, the TK’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, has refused to accept them. In May, the European Court of Human Rights ordered that the quartet be allowed to take up their positions. But the TK – where judges appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government retain a majority – issued its own ruling endorsing Nawrocki’s right not to swear in the new judges. On 11 June, the Sejm then chose another judge, Patyra, to fill a newly opened vacancy on the court. In his case, the legal doubts Nawrocki had expressed regarding the previous appointments, which in some instances were made more than a year after the vacancies had arisen, did not seem to apply. Yet for weeks the president refused to confirm whether he would swear him in. That prompted Patyra to write to Nawrocki in early July and then again this week, asking the president to indicate a date on which he could take his oath. Patyra himself has also made clear on which side of the dispute he stands. In an interview with news website Onet in May, he accused Nawrocki and Święczkowski of “blatantly unlawful actions” in deciding which TK judges can and cannot take office and suggested that the police should intervene. Sędzia TK prof. Patyra po raz kolejny zaapelował do Prezydenta o wyznaczenie mu terminu na złożenie przysięgi. Ignorowanie sędziego TK przez Prezydenta jest kolejnym przykładem psucia państwa. To pokazuje, jak bardzo siły anty-demokratyczne boją się odbudowy niezależnego TK.… — Dariusz Mazur (@_Dariusz_Mazur) July 21, 2026 Finally, on Wednesday this week, Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, announced that Nawrocki had invited Patyra to the presidential palace on Tuesday next week to take his oath. Speaking to Polsat News, Bogucki said that, in the case of Patyra, initially “there were some doubts, but the president dispelled them”, without specifying what they were. In the end, they concluded that “we had a fundamentally clean situation here” and Patyra was chosen “in accordance with all procedures”, unlike the six new judges chosen by the Sejm in March to fill longstanding vacancies. “It was not President Nawrocki or the current opposition who destroyed and are destroying the tribunal; it is the government that is doing it,” he added. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 The TK has been at the heart of the rule-of-law crisis that has developed in Poland over the last decade. In 2015, former PiS-aligned President Andrzej Duda refused to swear in three judges legally chosen by the Sejm. Shortly afterwards, PiS won parliamentary elections and nominated three replacements for those judges, who were sworn in by Duda. Those three judges and their successors have been deemed illegitimate in a succession of rulings by Polish and European courts. Due to their continued presence on the court, the current government, which replaced PiS in 2023, rejects the TK’s legitimacy and refuses to recognise its rulings. Under both Święczkowski, a former member of the PiS government, and his predecessor Julia Przyłębska, a close personal associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, the TK has been widely seen as issuing rulings aligned with the political interests of PiS. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Germany has deployed soldiers to Poland to help reinforce defences on NATO’s eastern flank in response to the threat of Russia. While Poland already hosts various allied forces, the presence of German troops is particularly symbolic given the two countries’ difficult history. “United, we will prevail,” wrote the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces (SGWP), announcing the deployment. “This is what allied cooperation looks like in practice, which translates into greater military readiness and strengthens NATO’s defensive potential.” Polscy i niemieccy żołnierze razem wzmacniają granicę z Rosją. Takie rzeczy możliwe tylko za Tuska ☺️ pic.twitter.com/oNBME2gBsv — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 22, 2026 Last December, the Polish and German defence ministries revealed that a “mid-double-digit number” of German troops would be deployed from mid-2026 until the end of 2027 to support implementation of Poland’s East Shield operation, which seeks to bolster defences along the borders with Belarus and Russia. They said that the German personnel would mainly engage in engineering work, such as digging trenches, laying barbed wire and constructing anti-tank barriers. Today, Poland’s SGWP confirmed that “several dozen” German troops, including “highly specialised engineering forces” along with their equipment, had since June been temporarily deployed to “support the Polish armed forces in expanding defence infrastructure on NATO’s northeastern flank”. It emphasised that the East Shield project is “purely defensive in nature” and comes in “response to threats stemming from, among others, Russian aggression against Ukraine”. While the armed forces did not reveal the location of the deployment, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk indicated in a social media post that it was on the Russian border. Poland has a 210-km frontier with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. German public broadcaster Deutsche Welle reports that the activities of the German sappers are focused in particular on improving defences around the so-called Suwałki Gap, a strategically important stretch of land around the Polish-Lithuanian border between Belarus and Kaliningrad. “Together, we are ensuring Europe’s security,” said Lieutenant General Alexander Sollfrank, the Bundeswehr’s operational commander, announcing the deployment today. “Through our engagement in Poland, we are strengthening NATO’s defence capabilities and underscoring the alliance’s unwavering commitment to ensuring peace through unity and credible deterrence.” Poland and Germany have signed a bilateral security agreement that will see the two neighbours and NATO allies increase cooperation in areas such as military mobility, logistics infrastructure, maritime security in the Baltic Sea, and cybersecurity https://t.co/6BPX2WxvxH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 17, 2026 SGWP, which shared footage of Polish and German forces installing anti-tank barriers, said the work aims to “hinder and delay an aggressor’s actions in the event of a threat”, thereby “increasing the time for a response from the Polish armed forces and the entire [NATO] alliance”. It also seeks to “create conditions for the efficient reception, deployment and use of NATO forces on Polish territory”. SGWP welcomed “the involvement of the German contingent as a practical expression of allied solidarity and the result of consistently developing military cooperation between Poland and Germany”. It also noted that the cooperation would help the two sides improve their ability to operate jointly, including “developing the competencies necessary for conducting a joint defence operation”. However, it emphasised that the current deployment is focused on training and engineering, with no combat component, and that the German troops are unarmed. SGWP also emphasised that the East Shield operation remains entirely a Polish national programme. The leaders of eight countries on the EU's eastern flank have met in the first summit of its kind to discuss closer security cooperation. Finland and Poland announced that they would jointly lead an initiative, Eastern Flank Watch, to bolster defences https://t.co/fxRHpkM6w9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 16, 2025 The deployment of German troops to Poland comes shortly after the two countries signed a defence cooperation agreement in which they pledged to increase cooperation in areas such as military mobility, logistics infrastructure, maritime security in the Baltic Sea, and cybersecurity. The agreement is a sign that the two countries now stand “shoulder to shoulder, as equals”, declared German defence minister Boris Pistorius. Poland is also currently seeking a new permanent US military base on its territory, after President Donald Trump recently pledged to boost American troop numbers. Last week, Tusk also announced that Poland will host military exercises involving France and the UK this autumn. Poland will host military exercises later this year with France and the UK to prepare for providing future security guarantees to Ukraine, says PM @donaldtusk. World.title: Easier after dark: Budapest expands night transport to a lot more suburbs
World.content:
From 1 August, getting home from Budapest at night will become significantly easier, as Hungary rolls out the next phase of its expanded suburban night transport network.

Announced by Transport Minister Dávid Vitézy, the development builds on July’s timetable overhaul and aims to connect even more towns and villages to the capital after midnight. The new services are synchronised with the last metro, HÉV, and train departures, ensuring smoother transfers and reducing waiting times for passengers travelling beyond Budapest’s city limits.

New direct routes from key hubs

A major highlight is the introduction of direct night connections from Kelenföld. These buses will serve Biatorbágy and continue to Sóskút, Pusztazámor and Etyek. From 11 August, additional routes from Kelenföld will reach Szigethalom, Halásztelek and Tököl, linking up with Metro Line M4.

In northern Budapest, a new night route will run from Újpest Városkapu all the way to Visegrád, passing through popular riverside settlements such as Szentendre, Leányfalu, Tahitótfalu and Dunabogdány.

The M4 metro line. Photo: BKK

North-west and north-east areas better connected

Transport links in the north-west will also improve. From Solymár, early-morning and night buses will connect to Pilisszentiván and Pilisszántó, timed to rail services. Meanwhile, from Pomáz, new connections will serve Pilisszentkereszt and Csobánka following the last H5 HÉV.

In the north-east, passengers travelling from the Stadion transport hub will gain access to Veresegyház and surrounding settlements, including Szada, Erdőkertes, Őrbottyán and Csomád. Services from Örs vezér tere will also run more frequently towards Csömör and Nagytarcsa.

Southern expansion reaches as far as Dabas

The southern agglomeration will see some of the most extensive upgrades. Night buses from Népliget will now run as far as Dabas, stopping at Alsónémedi, Ócsa, Inárcs, Kakucs and Újhartyán along the way.

A brand-new direct connection will also link Budapest with the Kiskunlacháza area. Until the Budapest–Belgrade railway line opens, buses will serve Dunaharaszti, Taksony, Dunavarsány and Délegyháza, continuing to Kiskunlacháza and even Dömsöd. Once the rail line is operational, the route will be adjusted to pass through Bugyi instead.

Stay up-to-date: Budapest public transport explained: Tickets, passes, fines and airport connections

A realistic alternative to driving

According to Vitézy, the expanded system is designed to be simple, predictable and competitive with car travel, even at night. With tens of thousands of commuters expected to benefit, the multi-phase rollout could transform how residents of the Budapest agglomeration travel after dark.

The minister emphasised that the long-term goal is a reliable, safe, and comprehensive night-time network that serves the needs of the region’s growing population.

World.title: 40 years without a break: Remarkable statistics from the Hungarian Grand Prix
World.content:
Very few countries can claim to have hosted more than 40 consecutive races at the same track and under the same name. The Hungaroring and the Hungarian Grand Prix are among them, and over four decades, they have produced some remarkable statistics. Several of the drivers currently on the starting grid secured their first victory here, and that’s just one of many interesting facts.

Author: Tamás Szikora

The first one is always special

Six drivers have celebrated their first Formula 1 victory at the Hungaroring, and three of them have since become world champions. Damon Hill triumphed in 1993 driving for Williams and went on to win the world championship three years later. Fernando Alonso, who competed as a Renault driver in 2003, started from pole position and crossed the finish line first; he then claimed his first world championship title in 2005, followed by another in 2006.

Jenson Button followed a similar path in this regard, though he had to wait quite a while for his first victory. He achieved this in 2006 while driving for Honda; surprisingly, this was the first rain-soaked race at the Hungaroring, and the British driver emerged from the chaos as the clear winner. Three years later, in 2009, Button finally became world champion with Brawn GP; to this day, he remains the last driver to win the world championship two or three years after his victory at the Hungaroring. In 2008, Heikki Kovalainen claimed his first and only F1 victory. In that race, Felipe Massa held a comfortable lead, but a few laps before the checkered flag, his Ferrari suffered a mechanical failure, allowing Kovalainen to inherit the victory.

In 2021, Esteban Ocon won a race that was particularly memorable and full of twists and turns due to the rain—this victory remains his only one to date. Then, in 2024, Oscar Piastri won the Hungarian Grand Prix. That race was no less memorable, as although Piastri was in the lead, McLaren’s strategy left him at a disadvantage compared to his teammate after the pit stops. The team eventually asked Lando Norris to let Piastri back in front of him, but the British driver was only willing to do so a few laps before the end of the race. This created a rather tense situation, but at the same time wrote another memorable chapter in Hungary’s racing history.

The track was completed in eight months

The Hungaroring was built in just eight months. Construction officially began in October 1985 and was fully completed by May 1986. This was a record at the time, and the track has undergone several renovations since then. One of the most significant renovations took place in 2003, when the Hungaroring was extended to 4,381 meters; the same track layout has been in use ever since, and major infrastructure improvements were completed this year. The main elements of these improvements were already in place by 2025, but the work was not fully completed until this year.

The Grand Prix held most frequently on the same circuit

If we consider only those races that have been held continuously from the very beginning, under the same name, and on a single circuit, the Hungaroring ranks first. Although the Hungarian Grand Prix ranks 11th on the list of the most frequently held races (as of Sunday) with 41 editions, the races ahead of it were often held at different tracks or with breaks in between. The Brazilian Grand Prix, for example, has so far been held at two different tracks and under two different names, but the British and Italian Grand Prix—which have been held every year since 1950—have also been held at multiple tracks. The Hungarian races, however, have always been held at the Mogyoród circuit, and fortunately, not a single year has been missed since 1986.

If you missed it: Three soccer players based in Hungary at the World Cup: everything you need to know

The record for the most pole positions at a single track

This record is also tied to the Hungaroring. Ahead of the 2026 race weekend, Lewis Hamilton has secured pole position a total of nine times in Hungary. Tied for second place in the rankings—each with eight pole positions—are Hamilton in Australia, Michael Schumacher in Japan, and Ayrton Senna at the San Marino Grand Prix. It is not impossible that the record for the most wins at a single track will also be set in Hungary in the future. Hamilton has won here eight times so far; the British seven-time world champion has achieved even greater success at a single venue, having won the British Grand Prix nine times.

World.title: Brace for another heatwave: Only a few cooler days left before extreme heat returns to Hungary
World.content:
Hungary has only a few days of relatively comfortable summer weather left before another long-lasting heatwave arrives, according to medium-range weather forecasts.

Forecasters say temperatures will begin rising steadily from next Tuesday, with early August expected to bring widespread highs above 35°C, while some areas could once again see temperatures close to 40°C. According to weather portal Időkép, current forecast models indicate that the hot spell could continue until at least 7 August, with no significant cooling in sight.

Pleasant weekend before the heat returns

Saturday is expected to be mostly sunny across Hungary, with only occasional thin and fair-weather clouds. No rainfall is forecast, and afternoon temperatures should reach 25–30°C, offering ideal conditions for outdoor activities.

Sunday will start with another relatively cool morning, with temperatures between 9°C and 19°C. During the afternoon, cloud cover will increase from the west, bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms first to western Hungary before spreading towards central and eastern parts of the country later in the day.

Strong southerly and south-westerly winds are expected in many areas, particularly across Transdanubia and central Hungary, while thunderstorms may produce locally severe gusts. Afternoon highs will range between 29°C and 34°C.

Heat builds rapidly next week

A cold front passing through on Monday may still trigger isolated showers and thunderstorms. However, meteorologists expect weather patterns to change quickly afterwards.

From Tuesday onwards, south-westerly airflows are forecast to bring increasingly hot air into the Carpathian Basin, causing temperatures to climb day by day.

According to Időkép, the first days of August are expected to bring persistent daytime temperatures well above 35°C across most of Hungary, with some locations potentially reaching or even exceeding 40°C.

Tropical nights expected to return

The heat will not be limited to daytime hours. Forecasters also expect nights to become progressively warmer, making restful sleep increasingly difficult. From the second half of next week,

temperatures in many parts of the country may remain above 20°C overnight, meeting the definition of so-called tropical nights.

Drought conditions likely to worsen

The returning heatwave is also expected to intensify Hungary’s ongoing drought. With scorching sunshine and little or no rainfall forecast for several consecutive days, soil moisture levels are likely to deteriorate further.

As Daily News Hungary reported, according to the latest data from HungaroMet, 90.2% of Hungary is currently experiencing at least moderate agricultural drought, highlighting the growing pressure on crops and water resources after an already exceptionally dry summer.

World.title: Shocking details emerge of Gáspár Orbán’s Chadian military mission: could many have died at immense cost?
World.content:
Fresh revelations have surfaced about one of the Hungarian state’s most opaque ventures in Africa’s Sahel region. Citing multiple independent sources, Magyar Hang reports that Gáspár Orbán was not merely a participant in the Chadian deployment but, from the outset, served as its commander in the rank of captain—despite the Orbán government having sought to deny the very existence of the intervention. Fellow soldiers reportedly described the “prince” as behaving like “a philosopher who had wandered onto a battlefield”.

Gáspár Orbán was to be reported to by all

According to Magyar Hang, on 20 September 2023, aboard a Hungarian Defence Forces Airbus departing from Kecskemét air base, Brigadier General Gábor Sánta announced after take-off that he would hand over command to “the Captain”, naming Gáspár Orbán as head of the Chadian mission. Accounts suggest members of the delegation reported directly to him.

This sharply contradicts earlier official communications. Kristóf Szalay-Bobrovniczky, then defence minister, had described Orbán merely as a “liaison” in an interview with Index, while former Chief of the General Staff Gábor Böröndi later said the Prime Minister’s son had participated for a time in a governmental planning group, adding that it was a “gross exaggeration” to claim he had led the mission. In parliament, Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi declined to comment on the new reports, stating only that an investigation is under way.

Magyar Hang reports that Gáspár Orbán spent extended periods in Chad, mostly in civilian dress, though at times in military uniform. One source said he behaved “like a philosopher straying into a military exercise”, frequently using his Iridium satellite phone, while some members of the team referred to him behind his back as “the prince”. The paper also claims that another captain’s insignia was removed to ensure no Hungarian of equal rank served alongside him.

Villa and accidents

A series of unusual incidents reportedly surrounded the mission. The Hungarian side, for instance, leased a villa on a long-term basis, intended to serve as a future embassy. Its furnishings were described by one source as “as if Győzike had been the interior designer”. Following refurbishment overseen by the security firm Inrimas, part of the team moved in; however, during the first evening’s showers, one Hungarian reportedly suffered an electric shock from stray current, prompting everyone to return to the hotel the following day.

PM Orbán and the Chadian President in Budapest in 2024. Photo: Facebook / Viktor Orbán

According to the paper, Inrimas—employing former soldiers and ex-Foreign Legion personnel—arrived in Chad before the Hungarian military to protect staff of the Hungary Helps humanitarian programme. Hungary Helps received 817 million forints in funding to open its Chadian office even before any official decision had been taken. Magyar Hang further reports that in 2024, ahead of presidential elections, local intelligence services searched the Hungarian delegation’s hotel rooms and seized small arms, bulletproof vests, a drone, thermal imaging equipment and other devices. This did not affect Hungarian soldiers, who were by then stationed at a French military base; however, the security firm has reportedly not had its equipment returned.

Hungarian universities linked to the mission

The mission, according to the paper, rested on four pillars: military, humanitarian, agricultural and investment cooperation. Óbuda University confirmed that, at the government’s request, it launched an English-language Humanitarian Response Manager course for Chadian participants over two academic years, receiving a total of 40.8 million forints in support. The Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences also acknowledged a presence in Chad but has yet to provide further details.

Parliament approved the Chadian military mission in November 2023. The government said it had been requested by the Chadian president, although the letter of request was not presented to the defence committee and was later obtained by Telex. While the official justification cited training Chadian forces, counter-terrorism efforts and curbing illegal migration towards Europe, the mission ultimately did not proceed.

Gáspár Orbán (l). Photo: PrtScr/Youtube/RTL

Hungary’s military mission to Chad leaked: “direct combat operations” were in plans

Did Gáspár Orbán anticipate half the force being lost?

A defence submission from November 2025, as reported by Magyar Hang, projected mission costs of more than 4 billion forints for 2026, alongside approximately 1.15 billion forints in national security spending and 21.8 billion forints in logistical expenditure. Earlier, Captain Szilveszter Pálinkás claimed that during their university years in London, Gáspár Orbán had told him the mission was calculated with a 50 per cent loss of combat effectiveness—in other words, the loss of half the Hungarian troops. Yet ahead of elections, the government also sought to deny that any Chadian mission had been planned at all.

Hungarian Defence Forces officer Captain Szilveszter Pálinkás. Screenshot: Telex/YouTube

Gáspár Orbán is the only son of Viktor Orbán, the former prime minister. He was previously a footballer and later led a charismatic Christian youth movement known as Felház. In the summer of 2019 he joined the military, and in 2020 was promptly sent on a state scholarship to the prestigious Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, alma mater of, among others, the heir to the British throne.

World.title: Budapest Danube boat carrying 85 passengers nearly sinks in city centre — video
World.content:
After seven hours of desperate efforts, teams from several authorities prevented the sinking of Táltos, a Hungarian Danube boat in Budapest. The incident was caused by extreme draught and the River Danube’s exceptionally low water level.

Desperate efforts to save Danube boat

According to Tények, TV2’s news programme, Táltos, one of the passenger boats regularly operating on the River Danube despite the extreme low water levels, almost sank near Budapest’s Elizabeth Bridge. As soon as the crew learned how serious the problem was from the Danube River Police Department, they began evacuating all passengers, which they completed swiftly and successfully.

Members of several authorities then arrived at the scene on Thursday evening to help keep the vessel afloat. At times, many feared the boat was beyond saving.

Officers from the Danube River Police Department, the Municipal Directorate for Disaster Management, and the Pest County Search and Rescue Service worked for more than seven hours to secure the boat.

Danube sightseeing cruises and family-themed boat trips launch for the season in Hungary!

No injuries

According to László Balázs, head of the Pest County Search and Rescue Service, the boat’s hull suffered multiple severe damages. The biggest hole in the hull was initially inaccessible, leaving the inflow of water seemingly unstoppable. Eventually, divers were able to repair it too.

Mr Balázs said the boat probably ran aground because of the River Danube’s extremely low water level and sustained further damage from rocks in the Danube bend.

Thankfully, no members of the crew or passengers were injured, and the rescue effort ended successfully.

New memorial site for deadly Hungarian boat tragedy

World.title: Hungaroring F1 highlights: Ferrari dominate opening day as Antonelli struggles
World.content:
Ferrari made an emphatic start to the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix weekend, with Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton topping the two Friday practice sessions at the Hungaroring. While the Italian team controlled the opening-day Hungaroring F1 highlights, championship leader Kimi Antonelli struggled for pace and confidence in his Mercedes.

Ferrari set the standard at the Hungaroring

Leclerc led the opening practice session with a lap of 1:19.075, finishing 0.484 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen. Hamilton took third place in the second Ferrari, giving the team an encouraging start at the circuit in Mogyoród, just outside Budapest.

The session did not end entirely smoothly for Leclerc. A mechanical problem forced him to stop near the pit-lane entrance during the final ten minutes, leaving Ferrari with additional checks to complete before FP2. Lance Stroll also suffered a rear-suspension failure, spinning his upgraded Aston Martin and causing a red flag.

Ferrari’s advantage became even clearer in the afternoon. Hamilton set the fastest lap of the day with a 1:18.729, beating Leclerc by 0.148 seconds and completing a Ferrari one-two. Lando Norris finished third for McLaren, followed by Verstappen and George Russell.

Formula 1’s official FP1 highlights and FP2 highlights show the main moments from Friday’s running.

Antonelli’s difficult first day in Hungary

Antonelli missed FP1 as Mercedes gave reserve driver Frederik Vesti an opportunity behind the wheel. Vesti finished seventh, while Russell placed fifth.

The championship leader returned for FP2 but encountered serious balance and braking problems. Antonelli reported that he had nearly spun twice under braking and repeatedly locked the rear wheels. He eventually finished only 13th, 1.964 seconds behind Hamilton and more than a second slower than Mercedes teammate Russell.

The second practice session was interrupted when Franco Colapinto lost control of his Alpine at the final corner and crashed backwards into the barrier. Stroll did not participate as Aston Martin continued repairing the damage caused by his FP1 suspension failure.

World.title: Large-scale, unexplained brown pollution contaminates Hungarian river — authorities respond, video, updated
World.content:
Efforts to remove a pollution discovered on Thursday in the River Fekete-Körös are set to begin on Friday afternoon, according to a statement issued by the Körös Regional Water Directorate (Kövizig) to the Hungarian news agency MTI. Preliminary results from official water samples are also expected to arrive later on Friday.

Preparations for on-site intervention are already under way, the authority said. Necessary fieldwork is being carried out to clear accumulated debris, ensuring that heavy machinery and transport vehicles can safely access the affected area.

The substantial mass of debris — believed, according to press reports, to be cattle manure — is currently stable. A submerged barrier installed to prevent its spread continues to contain the pollution, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

Water abstraction points within the Békés weir system remain temporarily closed, the statement added. Two designated bathing areas on the Körös rivers, at Szanazug and Városerdő, have been shut. Further measures will depend on laboratory analysis of water samples taken at multiple locations.

Water quality damage control operations continue under a third-degree alert level, the authority confirmed.

Later, the authorities said they had removed the pollution from the affected stretch of the river.

World.title: Other public institution, state-owned company heads dismissed by Magyar government – names revealed
World.content:
The Ministry of Social Relations and Culture has terminated the employment of the directors of the Natural History Museum, the National Széchényi Library and the Museum of Applied Arts, following a comprehensive institutional review of cultural background institutions, aimed at ensuring workplace safety, predictability and professional integrity. Furthermore, Minister István Kapitány fired the CEO of Paks II.

Three national collection heads sent away

The dismissal of Zsolt Bernert, Dávid Róza and Zoltán Cselovszki, respectively, came after a review which included consultations with institution leaders, works councils, representative bodies and dozens of employees, the ministry said in a statement quoted by the Hungarian news agency.

Minister Zoltán Tarr also ordered a comprehensive professional, economic and ethical internal investigation at the Hungarian National Museum’s Public Collection Centre (MNM KK), a supervising body of the museums.

The ministry has begun preparations to decentralise the MNM KK, enabling its affiliated institutions to operate with strengthened professional autonomy. The process will involve institution leaders, representative bodies and employees, with the goal of establishing a collection system that ensures a safe work environment, professional autonomy and long-term sustainable operations, the statement said.

Paks II CEO also sacked

Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said he had dismissed Gergely Jákli, the CEO of Paks II Nuclear Power Plant, in a post on Facebook on Friday. Kapitány said he would introduce the new CEO of the power plant expansion in the afternoon.

Hungarian lawyers’ circle head: former PM Orbán may soon become a suspect – can he be arrested?

World.title: Romanian director Alina Șerban’s debut film “I Matter” to premiere at Venice Film Festival
World.content:
“I Matter” (“Eu contez”), the feature film debut of Romanian director Alina Șerban (in photo), will have its world premiere at the 83rd edition of the Venice International Film Festival, taking place from September 1-12.

Written and directed by Alina Șerban, one of the few Roma female directors in the world, “I Matter” is a co-production between Romania (microFILM), Germany (2Pilots Filmproduction), and Belgium (Frakas Productions, Lemming Film), exploring themes such as overcoming fear, hope, and self-acceptance, according to the press release.

Spoken in Romanian and Romani, the film tells the story of Rebeca, a young Roma woman who is about to leave the foster care center where she grew up.

“We very rarely see Roma characters who live complex human experiences beyond stereotypes. And stories about what it means to be a girl, Roma, and part of the child protection system are almost nonexistent. Through ‘I Matter’ I wanted to build a bridge toward a deeper understanding of these experiences and, above all, to tell a story about humanity. The fact that this film is beginning its journey in Venice means a great deal to me,” said Alina Șerban.

The film was developed over more than four years together with young people from the social protection system. During this period, Alina Șerban created several documentary short films and theater performances alongside them.

The film’s cast includes Denisa Farcaș, Sorin Mihai, Angelina Pavel, Vanessa Dancea, Raisa Mihai, Juno (Alexandru Stancu), Alina Berzunțeanu, and Natalia Călin. Alongside them, 16 children and young people residing in the Casa Iosif and Casa Sara foster centers, part of the Măgurele Christian Social Ensemble in Bucharest, also appear in the film.

The Venice International Film Festival / Mostra Internazionale d'Arte Cinematografica will take place from September 2-12, 2026. “I Matter” has been selected alongside seven other titles in the Spotlight section, dedicated to audience films characterized by innovation and creativity in the way they engage with viewers. The film is competing for the Audience Award offered by Armani Beauty and the Luigi de Laurentiis Award for Best Debut, awarded by an international jury.

Winner of the Best Actress award at the German Actors’ Association Awards for her role in Gipsy Queen (2019), Alina Șerban is a graduate of the prestigious Tisch School of the Arts (New York), Royal Academy of Dramatic Art – RADA (London), and UNATC. In 2024, she was decorated by the president of Romania with the Order of Cultural Merit, in the rank of Knight.

She is the first Roma film and theater director in Romania and, for more than a decade, has developed artistic projects dedicated to children and young people from disadvantaged backgrounds, as well as Roma communities.

World.title: Anti-corruption prosecutors detain three directors of state-owned Romanian defense companies
World.content:
Romania’s National Anticorruption Directorate (DNA) officially announced on Friday, July 24, that it has detained three directors from companies within Romania's defense industry, all accused of taking bribes.

The three are Mihai Rafiu (general manager of Uzina Mecanică București), Tiberiu Alexandru Pîrvu (general manager of Uzina Mecanică Plopeni), and Liliana Sorescu (commercial director of Uzina Mecanică Plopeni).

Alongside the three, an administrator of several commercial companies was also detained, accused of giving bribes and complicity in giving bribes.

During searches, prosecutors found EUR 500,000 in cash at the home of Tiberiu Pârvu Alexandru. Authorities say Rafiu, for his part, allegedly received RON 48,000 from the businessman detained in this case, divided into 12 installments, according to the official DNA statement.

Tiberiu Pârvu Alexandru also allegedly received RON 25,900 from the same businessman "related to contracts concluded with the commercial companies effectively managed by defendant V.M."

The same businessman allegedly also bribed Liliana Sorescu. According to DNA, the total amount she allegedly received as bribes was RON 24,250, in several installments.

In addition, DNA also claimed that another businessman, who owns a company with contracts with Uzina Mecanică Plopeni, allegedly gave Liliana Sorescu USD 3,800, for "placing orders and carrying out the formalities necessary for the acceptance of the goods delivered by the respective companies."

Liliana Sorescu allegedly claimed that the dollars she received were counterfeit and requested the same amount once again, which she allegedly received in lei. "The contracts concluded by the two factories with the aforementioned commercial companies mainly concerned maintenance services, the purchase of materials, and the provision of services," DNA emphasized.

Reacting to the detention of the three directors, economy minister Irineu Darau said that "in general, the defense industry is an extremely sensitive subject. I am convinced that for some it is also a subject of temptation. A strong Romanian state must identify anyone connected to the defense industry who engages in dishonest activities.”

ROMARM, Romania's national state-owned defense company and the country's primary producer and exporter of military equipment, said in connection with the detention that it will support any legal action aimed at strengthening and reviving the defense industry.

The company noted that the problems within its subsidiaries have been known for some time and have been repeatedly brought to the attention of the Ministry of Economy, without answer.

The company's general manager, Răzvan Pîrcălăbescu, said in a statement cited by Digi24 that the reform plan was drafted by ROMARM's management, discussed with institutional partners, approved by the Board of Directors, and submitted to the Ministry of Economy for final approval, but so far the institution has made no decision.

World.title: Asia-born home improvement chain MR.DIY opens location at Bucharest’s Colosseum Mall
World.content:
MR.DIY, one of the world’s leading home improvement and lifestyle retailers, announced the opening of a location at Bucharest’s Colosseum Mall on Thursday, July 23.

Spanning over 800 sqm and developed following an investment of nearly half a million euros, the new MR.DIY store represents one of the most important openings within the retailer’s current national expansion plan, according to the press release.

The store offers a comprehensive one-stop-shop format offering customers access to thousands of practical everyday products across categories such as home improvement, household items, home organization, hardware and tools, stationery, toys, decorations, electrical accessories, car accessories and lifestyle products.

The opening is part of a process of diversification ongoing at the mall. Earlier this spring, Colosseum Mall also welcomed dm dogerie markt and Planeta Arthur bookstore.

The new store has been designed to deliver an accessible and efficient shopping experience, allowing customers to discover a broad assortment of products for everyday needs under one roof.

“This new store reflects our commitment to bringing the MR.DIY concept closer to Romanian consumers through accessible locations, a broad product assortment and affordable prices. Romania is an important market in MR.DIY’s European expansion strategy, and each new opening represents another step in building a strong long-term presence locally,” said Cătălin Secăreanu, representative of MR.DIY in Romania.

Established in Malaysia in 2005 with a single hardware store in Kuala Lumpur, MR.DIY has grown into one of Asia’s leading home improvement and lifestyle retailers, with a continuously expanding international presence across multiple markets. Today, MR.DIY operates in 15 countries worldwide, with more than 5,700 stores across Asia, Europe and other international markets.

World.title: EUR 80 million refinancing for Bucharest underground telecommunications network operator Netcity
World.content:
Meridiam and its partners have successfully closed the EUR 80 million refinancing of Netcity Telecom, the operator of Bucharest's underground telecommunications network, the company announced.

According to the company, the refinancing operation, led end-to-end by Meridiam, represents the first project finance bond issuance in the country, and establishes a new market record with tenors of up to 26.5 years, surpassing Meridiam's previous 18-year market benchmark achieved in 2022.

The operation also provides flexibility to support a future expansion of the Netcity Telecom network and new digital infrastructure developments across Bucharest, Meridiam said.

Netcity Telecom has been operating the underground telecommunications network in Bucharest since 2008, in a 49-year concession agreement with the Bucharest City Hall.

It has so far developed more than 3,000 kilometers of underground telecommunications infrastructure across Bucharest, while removing overhead cables. Today, the network serves around 70,000 buildings, representing approximately half of all buildings in the city, and provides internet access to nearly 600,000 homes and office premises.

Netcity Telecom has worked with several districts of Bucharest in designing and deploying dedicated fiber networks for municipal CCTV projects. The company has also contributed to the implementation of the pilot phase of the new Bucharest Traffic Management System, and is currently involved in Smart School initiatives.

Meridiam has an 80% stake in Netcity Telecom, alongside E-INFRA Group (20%), a Romanian group active in the energy, construction, and telecommunications sectors.

Meridiam, an independent investment Benefit Corporation and asset manager, was founded in 2005 by Thierry Déau. The firm specializes in the development, financing, and long-term management of public infrastructure across three sectors: sustainable mobility, critical public services, and innovative low-carbon solutions. With offices in Addis Ababa, Amman, Dakar, Istanbul, Johannesburg, Libreville, Luxembourg, Paris, Vienna, and Washington, Meridiam manages USD24 billion and more than 130 projects to date.

World.title: Romanian manufacturer TeraPlast inaugurates polyethylene pipe factory in Spain
World.content:
Romanian building materials manufacturer TeraPlast Group inaugurated its TeraPlast Iberia polyethylene pipe factory in Spain, strengthening its expansion into Western European markets. The facility, located near Bilbao, is expected to serve customers across Spain, France, and North Africa.

The factory, inaugurated on July 23, is located in Okondo, in Spain's Álava province, about 20 kilometers from Bilbao. It has an annual production capacity of 16,000 tonnes and employs 79 people.

The opening follows TeraPlast's acquisition of the facility and forms part of the group's international expansion strategy after earlier investments in the Republic of Moldova, Hungary, Austria, and Croatia.

“Romanian industry can compete and thrive at European level, and we demonstrate it through actions, not idealistic speeches. Following our expansion into the Republic of Moldova, Hungary, Austria and Croatia, our entry into the Spanish market marks another important step in our international growth strategy,” said Dorel Goia, chairman of the TeraPlast Board of Directors.

The company plans to invest EUR 4 million in the Spanish factory over the next three years to increase production by 60% and achieve an EBITDA margin of more than 10%.

“The expanded production capacity will serve the markets of Spain, France, and North Africa. This will enable us to reduce leverage while generating returns on our investment for the benefit of the group's shareholders," Goia added.

According to the company, the factory has an established customer base in Spain, France, and Germany and will serve as a regional hub for the group's operations in Western Europe.

TeraPlast Group is the largest polymer processor in Southeastern Europe and operates production facilities in Romania, the Republic of Moldova, Hungary, Austria, Croatia, and Spain. Its parent company, TeraPlast SA, is listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange under the symbol TRP.

World.title: Otokar starts deliveries of Romanian-built Cobra II armored vehicles
World.content:
Turkish defense manufacturer Otokar has begun delivering Cobra II tactical armored vehicles manufactured locally to the Romanian Armed Forces, marking the start of serial production at its plant in Mediaș. More than 780 of the 1,059 vehicles ordered by Romania are scheduled to be built at the local facility over the next five years.

The company said the first Cobra II vehicles manufactured entirely in Mediaș left the factory this week. A total of 216 vehicles, including four different variants, are scheduled for delivery in 2026.

The vehicles are being produced at Automecanica Mediaș, which has become Otokar's first manufacturing facility in the European Union. According to the company, the factory carries out the entire production process rather than only final assembly, giving Romania the capability to manufacture 4x4 armored vehicles locally.

“Romanian-made Cobra II deliveries have just begun. The first Cobra II vehicles manufactured entirely in Mediaș left the factory gates yesterday heading to the Romanian Armed Forces,” said Yusuf Fettahlıoğlu, General Manager of Automecanica Mediaş.

The Mediaș plant covers around 140,000 square meters and has been equipped to manufacture the vehicles to the same production standards as Otokar's facilities in Türkiye.

“Beyond the production line, the investment brings Romania what matters over the long term: advanced production know-how, technology transfer and engineering capabilities. The Mediaș plant is becoming a regional land-systems hub, capable of supporting not only production for the Romanian armed forces but also future export opportunities linked to NATO and European Union defence programmes,” stated Yusuf Fettahlıoğlu.

The Cobra II is a modular 4x4 tactical armored vehicle introduced in 2013 and currently used by more than 20 military and security organizations across 13 countries, including NATO members. For Romania, Otokar is producing several variants, including personnel carrier, reconnaissance, remote weapon station, CBRN reconnaissance, and ambulance versions.

The project has also expanded employment at the Mediaș facility, where the workforce now exceeds 300 people and is expected to grow to nearly 400 as production ramps up.

(Photo source: the company)

World.title: Romania wins one gold, seven silver medals at first Central European Olympiad in AI
World.content:
The Romanian delegation to the first Central European Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (CEOAI), held in Cluj-Napoca between July 14-19, won one gold medal and seven silver medals, according to the Ministry of Education.

The event represented a historic moment for the international AI community, bringing together more than 90 contestants from over 20 European countries, along with invited delegations from around the world.

During the competition, contestant had to design, train, and optimize their own artificial intelligence models, starting from completely new datasets and requirements. In the two competition days, students tackled problems in diverse fields, such as artificial intelligence model interpretability, optical character recognition (OCR), mathematical and physical modeling, computer vision, and the security of machine learning models through steganography techniques. The competition tested not only the participants' technical knowledge but also their creativity, analytical ability, and rapid adaptation to problems without standard solutions, according to G4Media.

Following the interest shown by high school students from across Europe, the competition, initially known as the Central European Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (CEOAI), received a new name, becoming the European Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (EUROAI).

Emil-Andrei Burloi, a student at the International Computer Science High School of Bucharest, ranked third in the overall competition standings, winning Romania's first gold medal in international AI competitions in 2026. Subsequently, following the decision of the Ministry of Education and Research for the Romanian delegation to participate as a guest delegation, the official ranking was adjusted in accordance with the competition regulations.

Silver medals went to Ciortea-Suciu Andrei from the "Silvania" National College, Zalău, Morariu Tudor from the International Computer Science High School of Bucharest, Ilie-Goga Radu from the "Tudor Vianu" National College of Computer Science Bucharest, Dobre Darius-Adrian from the "Matei Basarab" National College of Computer Science in Râmnicu Vâlcea, Apostol Mihnea-Petru from the same highschool, Nistor Iulian from the “Tiberiu Popoviciu" Computer Science High School in Cluj-Napoca, and Asandei Ștefan-Alexandru from the Iași National College.

The national team was coordinated by Miron Radu (Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iași) and Ciprian Păduraru (University of Bucharest). The national team's qualification was achieved following the ROAI stages, organized in partnership with Genesis College and the "Tudor Vianu" National College of Computer Science, with the support of the Nitro Association, Babeș-Bolyai University, the University of Bucharest, and Alexandru Ioan Cuza University of Iași.

Throughout the selection stages, hundreds of students from across the country solved original machine learning and deep learning problems, training their own models and demonstrating advanced skills in a field at the intersection of computer science, mathematics, and research.

World.title: Romania to receive EUR 2.15 bln in NATO funding for fuel pipeline network expansion
World.content:
President Nicușor Dan announced on Thursday, July 23, that following more than five years of negotiations, NATO approved the eastward expansion of its fuel pipeline network, a strategic result for Romania.

The Alliance will fund the expansion with EUR 27 billion over the next 20 years, of which Romania will receive EUR 2.15 billion. The new network will also cross Romanian territory, will have both military and civilian uses, and will create important opportunities for the Romanian economy and companies.

"Romania achieves an important strategic result within NATO. After more than five years of negotiations, the Alliance has approved the eastward expansion of NATO’s fuel pipeline network, an essential project for strengthening security and military mobility on the Eastern Flank. The decision also comes as a result of lessons learned after Russia invaded Ukraine, which demonstrated how important logistical infrastructure is for collective defense,” the president said on Facebook.

Romania has been actively involved from the very beginning in the negotiation, through the efforts of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of National Defence, and Romania’s Delegation to NATO, according to the head of state.

“This project strengthens Romania’s role as a frontline allied state on the Black Sea and enhances our country’s strategic connectivity with NATO allies,” Dan said.

Specifically, the NATO Fuel Supply Chain Capability Program will modernize NATO’s existing fuel storage and distribution infrastructure. “It will support new facilities, including pipelines, in the eastern and south-eastern part of the Alliance and ensure NATO forces have the energy supplies they need for warfighting readiness,” according to the NATO press release.

The investment is part of NATO’s 2027–2031 Common Funding Resource Plan, which sets out how the Alliance will invest in shared priorities over the next five years. As part of the decision, Allies agreed the 2027 funding ceilings for NATO’s Military Budget, Civil Budget and Security Investment Programme, raising total common funding to up to EUR 6.5 billion.

The plan also provides resources for priority support to Ukraine, including the NATO Security Assistance and Training to Ukraine initiative and the NATO-Ukraine Joint Analysis, Training and Education Centre.
